## What worked

- Cross-examination paid off. Sol's final wrongly said the facade was complete. A neutral follow-up naming `KeyboardPanel` and the shared `shell/Ui` consumers (without quoting Opus) made Sol find and retract it. It also independently confirmed five more Opus-only claims.
- The Opus sandboxed run used the base as a positive control, which made F2 easy to trust.

## Friction and deviations
- Opus reviewer: one intermediate grep list was first written to the CLI session scratchpad and then moved into `opus/work/` (recorded in `opus/RETRO.md`). It was an owned, non-evidence artifact. The public claims do not depend on it.

- The coordinator's Opus prompt followed the runtime section's fixed wording. The first-call rules live at the top of `brief.md`, not in the prompt itself. Earlier audit corrections asked for them in the dispatch, but the current runtime section prescribes the exact prompt. Worth reconciling in the workflow.
- The coordinator started a 600 s timer for Sol status checks. Sol finished in 8.9 minutes, so no mid-run check was needed.

## Improvements
- Provide a hashed standalone `node` in review.py fixtures so Node-based shell tests (`bar-test.sh`, `plugin-auth-boundary-test.sh`) can run.
- Brief template: suggest that reviewers enumerate transitive consumers of injected objects (shared UI components), since the main defect was one hop away.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

The defaults do not fully preserve existing behavior. Handing first-party widgets a per-monitor bar object drops `clickTargets`. With both new options at `false`, this breaks one-click switching between bar panels and fails an existing shell test. The opt-in per-monitor foreground can also make popup text match the popup background.

**Verified** (source review against Quickshell and Hyprland source):

- Both new keys default to `false` in `config/omarchy/shell.json` and `fallbackBarConfig`, and are read with `=== true`, so existing user configs without them behave as `false`.
- Each bar surface paints its background from its own monitor (`Hyprland.monitorFor(screen)`), not the focused one. A visible special workspace with windows keeps that monitor's bar solid; a hidden one does not count.
- `BarModel.specialWorkspaceEvent` matches the shapes Hyprland emits: `activespecial` as `NAME,MON` / `,MON` and `activespecialv2` as `ID,NAME,MON` / `,,MON`.
- `omarchy-bar-text-color` already accepts `--screen WxH`, and the helper output is checked against `^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$` before use.

### First-party keyboard panels lose one-click switching to another bar icon

`ModuleSlot.injectProps` now gives first-party widgets `root.slotWindow(slot)`, the per-screen `BarPanel`, instead of `root`, in every configuration (`shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml:2159-2167`). The `BarPanel` stand-in (`Bar.qml:1306-1350`) forwards most of the bar API but has no `clickTargets`. First-party panels (audio, network, bluetooth, clock, power, monitor, tailscale, weather, dropbox, agents) pass that `bar` to `KeyboardPanel`, which needs it to forward clicks on the bar strip:

```text
panel open, click on another bar icon
  KeyboardPanel.onClicked
    forwardBarClick -> pressTargetAt
      base: root.bar.clickTargets = [registered buttons] -> target.triggerPress() -> new panel opens
      head: root.bar.clickTargets = undefined -> return null -> root.close()   (second click needed)
```

(`shell/Ui/KeyboardPanel.qml:302-331`)

Button registration still reaches `root.clickTargets` through the forwarded `registerClickTarget`, so only the read side is missing. No other member that first-party code or the shared `shell/Ui` components read from `bar` is missing.

**Impact:** with the new options off, every first-party panel now needs two clicks to switch to another bar panel. Established from source; not observed on a desktop.

**Suggested change:** add `readonly property var clickTargets: root.clickTargets` to `BarPanel`. Alternatively, keep passing `root` to first-party widgets and expose the per-surface state separately.

### Existing shell test fails on this head

`test/shell.d/plugin-auth-boundary-test.sh:88-92` asserts the literal `target.bar = firstParty ? root : root.pluginBarApiFor(...)`. The head now reads `? (barSurface || root) :`, so the file exits 1 with `not ok - third-party widgets receive a bar facade instead of the host bar`. The static portion of the test was run in a sandbox: all 11 groups pass on the merge-base, and the head fails at this group. The third-party branch itself is unchanged, so this is a test-contract mismatch, not a third-party exposure. `shell/plugins/bar/README.md` ("Widgets receive `bar` (the shell root)") describes the same contract.

**Suggested change:** once the facade question above is settled, update the assertion and the README to the new first-party contract.

### `transparentForegroundPerMonitor`: popup text can match the popup background

With the option on and the bar transparent, `BarPanel.foreground` becomes the wallpaper-selected colour (`Bar.qml:1316-1317`), not the theme text colour. First-party panels use `bar.foreground` for content on their own popup card (for example `panels/clock/Panel.qml:78`, `panels/weather/Panel.qml:540`, `shell/Ui/PanelSlider.qml`).

| | Colour |
| --- | --- |
| Helper candidates | `Color.bar.text` or `Color.background` |
| Popup card background | `Color.popups.background`, which defaults to `Color.background` (`shell/Commons/Color.qml:78-81`) |
| Panel text when the helper picks the contrast colour | `Color.background`, the same as the card |

**Impact:** a dark theme with a bright top strip in the wallpaper can make panel labels, icons and slider fill invisible. Established from source; not rendered.

**Suggested change:** keep `foreground: root.foreground` on the facade and let only `barForeground` follow the per-monitor sample.

### `transparentOnlyWhenWorkspaceEmpty`: stale special-workspace state after enabling at runtime

The `activespecial` listener runs only while the option is on (`Bar.qml:1162-1170`), and `visibleSpecialWorkspaceNames` takes priority over `lastIpcObject.specialWorkspace`, which Quickshell does not refresh on special-workspace events. Sequence: open a populated scratchpad with the option on, turn it off, hide the scratchpad, turn it on again. The stored name still points at the hidden, populated workspace. The reverse case is a scratchpad shown while the option is off.

**Impact:** after the option is toggled at runtime, a bar can stay solid on an empty monitor, or transparent over a shown scratchpad, until the next special-workspace toggle. Established from source; not observed on a desktop.

**Suggested change:** track the special-workspace events regardless of the option, or clear and re-fetch monitor state when it is enabled.

### Smaller notes

- **Existing `transparent: true` setups:** the base kept the bar solid until the helper returned a text colour. The head clears the background immediately and shows theme text until the 120 ms timer and helper finish (`Bar.qml:1310, 1426`). This contradicts the comment at `Bar.qml:1098-1099`, and if the helper never returns a colour, the bar now stays transparent. Transient in the normal case.
- **Helper reruns on unrelated events:** in workspace mode every Hyprland raw event, including title changes on other workspaces, schedules `syncTransparency()`. While the focused workspace is empty, that relaunches `omarchy-bar-text-color` (ImageMagick) after each burst. Filtering to window, workspace, special-workspace and monitor events would avoid this. CPU cost not measured.
- **Mixed monitors:** third-party widgets (`PluginBarApi`, `Bar.qml:130-145`) and drag ghost/border chrome still take `transparent` and `barForeground` from the focused monitor. For example, a third-party widget on a solid monitor can get the contrast colour chosen for an empty focused monitor. Without the per-monitor option, an empty unfocused monitor also shows theme text whenever the focused monitor has windows.
- **`--screen` size:** `HyprlandMonitor.width/height` are physical, untransformed mode pixels, while `barSize` is logical. A rotated or scaled monitor is sampled from the wrong region or too thin a strip. `barWindow.screen.width/height` gives the logical, oriented size.
